title: Wildfire Exposure Assesment For Algerian Barbary Macaques (Macaca sylvanus)
text:
The Barbary Macaque (Macaca sylvanus)  is North Africa’s only primate and has been classified as endangered by the IUCN Red list as of 2008. The species occupies a small and heavily fragmented range within forested regions of Morocco and Algeria, along with a small introduced population on Rock of Gibraltar. It faces critical threats from deforestation, urbanization, agriculture, and human disturbances driven by tourism.





Barbary Macaques pictured in the Chiffa Gorge in Blida, Algeria. Photo: Louiza Mohamed-Cherif




Algeria holds nearly 25% of the Barbary Macaque’s population, however there is a crucial need for new reviews of Algerian macaque populations as a recent comprehensive census of the existing populations within the country does not exist (Boumenir et. al , 2025). Even more pressing, recent dry seasons driven by climate change have worsened regional wild fires, which overlap with Algerian macaque habitat.





A wildfire across a forested mountain in Northeast Algeria. Photo: Hafid Derradji/Facebook via Morocco World News




In the summer of 2026 nearly 160 wildfires broke out along the northeastern coast of Algeria. This study aims to map the spatial intersection of 2026 wildfire damage with known macaque habitat to estimate recent habitat loss.

2. Calculating total habitat burned

burned_sf <- st_make_valid(burned_sf)
habitat_sf <- st_make_valid(habitat_sf)
#1. Calculate the overlap of burned area and macaque habitat 
burned_hab_union <- st_union(burned_sf) # 1.1 combine burned area into one combined total 
burned_hab_union <- st_make_valid(burned_hab_union)
# 1.2 intersect burned area with habitat 
burned_hab <- st_intersection(burned_hab_union, habitat_sf)
# 1.2.1 - check by running plot(burned_hab)
# 1.3 calculate total area burned 
burned_area <- burned_hab |> 
  st_as_sf() |>  # 1.3.1 convert burned_hab back into an sf before passing to st_area 
  mutate(burned_area = st_area(x)) # 1.3.2 x notates the single column in burned_hab 

# burned_area is approx. 40.5km2 
# 1.4 find percent habitat burned 

percent_burned <- (as.numeric(burned_area$burned_area)/as.numeric(hab_area))*100 

# percent_burned -- they lost 6.23% of habitat in the northeast in ONE SUMMER! That's not good!
